items.issues: Pencil rule pays off with the pencil-addressed letter kept back; B is the local-reading trap, C/D are passage-grounded but miss the whole-text function.
C is a good trap (tea is a gesture, but the notebooks turned toward her are the payoff); A inverts the meaning, D is the generic reading.
B tempts because the sentence after the underline states Shuang's view; C requires reading the boot payments and the final slowed step. Clean.
C is partly defensible ('not lying, exactly' hints guilt and he did doubt the plan), but the guilt is about the lie, not toward Casey; B's grumbling/affection split matches the ending best.
B's 'make up for her own past' and A's 'shared humor' have no textual basis; D is the surface reading. Note narrator gender never stated, B assumes 'her'.
B is directly contradicted (father would let her off); A/C take the jokes at face value. Flag-fold and jacket make D fairly evident, so medium rather than hard.
Opening rhetorical question plus the coffee/vines ending make the trajectory clear; D has the direction right but the wrong dominant term. Solid.
Coiling cable 'the way he coiled it' signals respect; C's 'dutiful gratitude' and D's 'weary tolerance despite finding him impossible' are internally weak as contrasts.
D is the strongest trap (she does take up the routine) but misses that the absence is the point; A and B are partial-passage ideas. Good hard item.
Requires reading spanner handoff plus canvas bag together; C is a causal inversion, A/B are partial. Clean.
D inverts cause (the price was deliberate, not a consequence); B and C are partial truths. Apprentice gender unstated but B says 'her'; minor.
'Did not argue or apologize' rules out A; careful letter-by-letter correction rules out B/C. Two constraints (cares about error, no outward display) point to D only.
A fits the 'though' contrast with the narrator's chill, but 'accepting' sits oddly with her asking Hedwig to keep working anyway; B/C/D are eliminated quickly, so more medium than hard.

B wins by elimination, but 'frank' is weakly supported: nothing shows her saying anything candid about the mistake, only calm acceptance. Consider 'unexpectedly easy/untroubled'. C and D are thin distractors.
A wrong direction, B wrong cause, D wrong degree; the unlabeled cloth gift as release is subtle. Well built.
Rule-then-pocketing-the-card is a very legible setup/payoff; D is unsupported, A/C are local-only. Reads as medium.
The name Lara returning on the tape makes C clear; A and D are local readings of the underline, B misdescribes the structure. Medium.
B describes the narrator's reaction at the time, not the sentence's function in the whole text; the stubs reversal is the hinge. Good trap, moderate difficulty.
Lowest shelf for a bad back plus larger price numbers = protective care; B's 'guilty' is unsupported ('not saying I was hurt'), D answers a different question. Clean.
